findings.title: Render Bishop defenders with their artwork
findings.why_it_matters: In a normal legal Bishop-vs-Bishop capture, the new Bishop identity reaches the existing resolver, but the resolver does not return Bishop art. The presenter therefore replaces the actual opponent with a lettered B placeholder, despite this batch providing an illustrated ready pose. For example e4 e6 d4 d5 Bf4 Bd6 Bxd6 has Hiccup capture Killer; the impact and reaction display a generic badge rather than Killer. This fails the established knight-defender pattern and makes the newly introduced character identity disappear at the moment of the reaction.

findings.suggested_fix: Apply a bounded timeout to the Bishop file requests or the load operation, cancel the completion listener on timeout, and call the existing unavailable fallback exactly once; test stalled responses and late completion after timeout.
findings.title: Bound stalled Bishop artwork requests
findings.why_it_matters: A first Bishop capture can remain on ‘Getting ready’ with board input locked indefinitely when an artwork request stalls rather than returning an error. Skip is available, but the move does not complete naturally, and Phaser's default XHR timeout is zero. A bounded load timeout that detaches the listener and invokes the existing failure fallback would restore progress without requiring the player to diagnose a stalled download.
findings.validation_reason: When an artwork request stalls, the snapshot waits exclusively for loader COMPLETE at bishopAssets.ts:16 while AttackScene.ts:189-192 starts or skips only in that callback; Phaser's Config.js:531 defaults timeout to zero and XHRLoader.js:58 uses it, with no project override found, so natural completion remains blocked unless the user skips; incidence was not measured.

findings.suggested_fix: Track completion and failure for the requested keys rather than waiting for the global loader COMPLETE event, or cancel and remove the abandoned requests; exercise Skip followed by a different Bishop capture while the first response remains held.
findings.title: Skipped downloads block subsequent Bishop captures
findings.why_it_matters: If a player skips a capture while one artwork request is stalled and then triggers another Bishop capture, the second capture remains locked in the preparing state until the abandoned request finishes. Cancelling detaches only the old callback, and the new callback waits for the shared loader’s global completion, which requires every pending and in-flight file, including the skipped capture’s files. The player can skip again, but cannot see the new capture while the unrelated request hangs.
findings.validation_reason: When a cold request remains in flight after Skip, the snapshot's bishopAssets.ts:16-18 only removes its callback; Phaser LoaderPlugin.js:1119-1121 emits global completion only after all pending, in-flight and processing files finish, so a later capture's callback also waits on the abandoned request; the precise incidence was not measured.

triage_groups.title: Artwork loading and cancellation
triage_groups.context: Both issues arise from waiting on the shared loader.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Isolate or cancel capture requests and bound their wait.
triage_groups.why: A stalled or abandoned load can delay a later capture.

triage_groups.title: Presentation fidelity and verification
triage_groups.context: Named defenders and actual phases need explicit coverage.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Load named Bishop defenders and assert actual animation phases.
triage_groups.why: A completed move alone does not establish that the scene played.

requirements.note: Four attacker scenes and art are represented; finding 2 addresses defender depiction.
Identity and lifecycle paths exist; findings 3 and 4 concern stalled and abandoned loads.
Capture tests and recording scripts exist; finding 1 strengthens assertions. Binary recordings were excluded from this review.
Previous knight approval documentation is updated; draft PR and owner acceptance are delivery steps outside this pre-fix review.

implementation_units.note: Finding 1 and later delivery; recordings excluded from code review.

residual_risks: Owner visual acceptance and physical-phone performance remain separate from automated tests, as AGENTS.md requires.
The 14 Bishop WebP textures are retained in the shared Phaser texture manager after use; their cumulative decoded memory and mobile performance remain unmeasured.
testing_gaps: The cold-load Skip regression did not wait for the held requests to complete before asserting that no late callback resumed presentation.

notes: Artwork and recordings were excluded from the code diff and inspected separately.
The reviewed pre-fix tree is available in snapshot/.
